papers.title: Best1 shapes the depth and stability of NREM sleep.
papers.abstract: Sleep architecture is orchestrated by neuronal circuits, yet the contribution of astrocytes-particularly to the depth and continuity of sleep-remains incompletely understood. Mammalian sleep is composed of rapid eye movement (REM) and non-REM (NREM) stages, with NREM further subdivided into light and deep phases. While neuronal and neurotransmitter-based mechanisms of sleep regulation have been extensively characterized, the role of astrocytic signaling in deep NREM sleep has received relatively little attention. Bestrophin-1 (Best1) is a calcium-activated anion channel highly enriched in astrocytes, known to mediate non-vesicular release of gliotransmitters such as glutamate, D-serine, and GABA, and to influence neuronal excitability. Here, we identify Best1 as a critical regulator of deep NREM sleep. Immunohistochemistry revealed robust Best1 expression in astrocytes across sleep-regulating brain regions. EEG/EMG polysomnography in Best1 knockout (Best1-KO) mice demonstrated a selective disruption of deep NREM sleep, despite preserved total sleep time and overall NREM duration. Best1-KO mice exhibited shorter deep NREM bouts, attenuated delta-band (0.5-4 Hz) EEG power, and altered vigilance-state transitions, with reduced entry into and maintenance of deep NREM. Sleep trajectories were biased toward Wake → light NREM → REM transitions, frequently bypassing deep sleep stages. Spectral decomposition further confirmed diminished delta oscillations during NREM episodes. These findings establish Best1 as a substage-specific molecular gatekeeper of deep NREM sleep. By uncovering a glial mechanism that shapes sleep sub-architecture, this work highlights astrocytic ion signaling as a promising therapeutic target for disorders marked by fragmented or insufficient deep sleep, including those associated with aging and neurodegenerative disease.

papers.title: Slow-Wave Enhancement Reduces Axonal Injury in Murine Traumatic Brain Injury.
papers.abstract: Traumatic brain injury (TBI) is a major cause of death and disability as well as impaired cognition and sleep-wake abnormalities. The pathological hallmark of TBI is disturbed axonal transport and accumulation of proteins, leading to diffuse axonal injury (DAI). Recent studies suggest a role for slow-wave sleep (SWS) in the clearance of harmful extracellular proteins and functional recovery. Our group previously found that increasing SWS after TBI in rats improved cognition and decreased accumulation of injury-related histological markers in cortex and hippocampus, indicating a neuroprotective role of SWS. Though growing evidence suggests that sleep can improve the outcome of TBI, prior mouse models of TBI were incompatible with sleep recordings. In the current study, we modified the classical weight-drop mouse model to be compatible with a headset for recording electroencephalogram (EEG) and electromyogram, and to replicate effects of SWS modulation on TBI outcome measures. The resulting mild TBI mouse model shows cognitive impairment, EEG abnormalities, and DAI. Such DAI was reduced following treatment with sodium oxybate during the first 3 days after trauma, concomitant with increased slow-wave activity. Chemogenetic modulation of basal forebrain cholinergic neurons, on the other hand, did not reduce slow-wave activity. Overall, in the present study, we characterized an adapted weight-drop mouse TBI model for studying the relationship between sleep and TBI and provided additional evidence on involvement of sleep in neuronal recovery.

papers.title: Neural mitochondria size is negatively correlated with sleep duration.
papers.abstract: Discharge of fruit fly sleep-promoting neurons is coupled to mitochondrial activity1. In vertebrates, adenosine accumulation resulting from adenosine triphosphate metabolization triggers sleep2. Such observations and theoretical considerations3,4 prompted us to investigate the link between neural mitochondria and sleep duration. To this end, we measured mitochondrial cross-sections in electron microscopy micrographs from publications of nerve or brain mitochondria in 51 mammalian species. There was considerable within-species variability of mitochondrial cross-section areas and we only included species where measurements from at least two publications could be made. Across 50 of the 51 species the average neural mitochondrial cross-section area decreased roughly exponentially with sleep duration (r = -0.76, p < 0.0001). The naked mole rat was an outlier having large brain mitochondria and long sleep. We also observed a significant decrease of sleep duration with body weight, and a multiple linear regression using sleep duration and body weight explained about 64% of the variance of mitochondrial cross-section areas. We suggest that the urge to sleep might be biophysically linked to mitochondrial size and mitochondrial leakage. Specifically, size-related decreases of mitochondrial surface-to-volume-ratio might reduce the need for sleep by decreasing mitochondrial leakage of reactive oxygen species (ROS). We identify neural mitochondrial size as a possible cellular determinant of sleep duration.

papers.title: Intra-thalamic coordination maintains arousability in slow-wave sleep
papers.abstract: Slow-wave sleep preserves the capacity for spontaneous or stimulus-evoked awakening despite reduced responsiveness, yet how thalamic nuclei coordinate to preserve arousability remains unclear. We analysed six fMRI and EEG datasets spanning sleep, propofol anesthesia and unresponsive wakefulness syndrome (UWS). During N2 and N3, centromedian (CM) and ventral posterolateral (VPL) nuclei showed convergent edge-community profiles and increased closed-loop intra-thalamic motifs, changes not observed during anesthesia or UWS. During N3, directed effective connectivity along CM[->]VPL[->]pulvinar (PUL) increased versus wakefulness and N2. Stronger CM[->]VPL and VPL[->]PUL connectivity covaried with greater N3 delta power, which was higher before awakening than before transitions to N2 and positively associated with three-month improvement in behavioural responsiveness in UWS. These findings identify a CM-VPL-PUL-centred pattern of intra-thalamic organization linked to preserved arousability during slow-wave sleep, extending accounts focused on individual nuclei and thalamocortical interactions.

papers.title: Multiple platform-induced sleep restriction disrupts time-of-day-dependent corticosterone and leukocyte profiles in C57BL/6 mice.
papers.abstract: Sleep restriction (SR) is recognized to alter neuroendocrine and immune parameters, yet whether these changes reflect overall alterations in signal magnitude or temporal shifts in systemic dynamics remains poorly defined. We evaluated the effects of subchronic sleep restriction on the 24-h diurnal profiles of serum corticosterone (CS), total white blood cell (WBC) counts, and granulocyte-enriched proportions in mice. Male C57BL/6 mice were subjected to subchronic sleep restriction using the multiple-platform procedure or maintained under control conditions. Serum CS, total circulating WBC counts defined by FSC/SSC gating, and granulocyte-enriched percentages were measured across distinct Zeitgeber times and analyzed using two-way ANOVA with Holm corrections for multiple testing. Daily mean corticosterone levels and total WBC counts did not differ significantly between groups. A significant treatment × time interaction occurred for serum CS (p < 0.001), but time-point differences lost significance after Holm correction (p ≥ 0.06). Total WBC counts showed a borderline interaction (p = 0.050) with no time-point differences post-correction ≥, and CS-WBC correlations were not significant (p > 0.05). Conversely, granulocyte-enriched percentages exhibited a significant interaction (p = 0.002) and retained significant group differences post-correction at ZT5 (36.07 ± 2.57% vs. 18.10 ± 5.59%, adjusted p = 0.005) and ZT11 (53.03 ± 0.21% vs. 84.86 ± 8.64, adjusted p = 0.006). The multiple-platform procedure is associated with time-specific differences in serum CS and granulocyte-enriched percentages without altering the diurnal mean CS or total WBC counts. Lacking direct mechanistic measurements, these data reflect potential temporal variations under sleep restriction paradigms rather than established corticosterone-mediated regulation, clock disruption, or altered tissue homing.

papers.title: Rest promotes microglial clearance of degenerating neurons
papers.abstract: How the brain coordinates the removal of degenerating neurons with host rest and activity remains poorly understood. Using longitudinal two-photon imaging in mice with cytosolic TDP-43 proteinopathy, we show that microglia remove neuronal corpses through an ordered sequence of reaching, approaching, isolating and digesting. Clearance was higher during the light (resting) phase and lower during the dark (active) phase. This pattern reversed after light-dark cycle inversion and was blunted by sleep disruption. Chemogenetic inhibition of locus coeruleus noradrenergic neurons increased engulfment during the active phase, while activation and inhibition of the {beta}2-adrenergic receptor ADRB2 suppressed and enhanced clearance, respectively, identifying noradrenergic signaling as a brake on engulfment. However, sustained microglial ADRB2 deletion impaired clearance and blunted light-dark differences. These findings reveal that microglial removal of degenerating neurons is enhanced during rest and support a role for noradrenergic signaling in coordinating this cellular maintenance process with the host's rest-activity cycle.

papers.title: Comparison of Infradian and Circadian Rhythms in Laboratory Rodents.
papers.abstract: Infradian cycles are multi-day oscillations whose mechanisms are still poorly understood, while circadian rhythms have been extensively studied and are well-documented in mammals. In this study, we monitored the locomotor activity of three rodent species: CD-1 mice (Mus musculus), Mongolian gerbils (Meriones unguiculatus), and white-tailed antelope squirrels (Ammospermophilus leucurus). We used Lomb-Scargle spectral analysis to verify the prevalence of circadian and infradian rhythms, the magnitude of the spectral power, and associations across species, rhythms, and sexes. Circadian rhythms were robust and were found for all animals. For infradian rhythms, the prevalence in mice was extremely low, whereas the prevalence in gerbils and squirrels was moderate in the 5- and 10-day ranges. In all cases, the strength of infradian rhythmicity was less than 10% of the strength of circadian rhythmicity. As no natural environmental cycle is documented to operate in the 5- to 10-day range, further studies are needed to determine whether an endogenous source may account for this weak but significant infradian rhythmicity.

papers.title: Deciphering the impact of chronological age on sleep stage transition dynamics for disorder classification.
papers.abstract: Ageing and sleep disorders are closely linked, as physiological changes can increase sleep fragmentation in older adults. Although sleep stage transition probability (STP) features provide useful markers of sleep disruption, age-related variability presents challenges for generalised sleep disorder classification. This study investigated the influence of chronological age on sleep disorder detectability and compared age-agnostic, age-involved, and age-specific machine learning (ML) approaches. Using single-night hypnograms across three data groups, two-stage STP features were extracted and evaluated through five experimental configurations, including models without age information, models incorporating age as a feature, and models stratified by age group. Statistical validation using absolute differences between transition probability matrices was performed to assess healthy-disordered differences across age cohorts and thresholds. Age-involved models provided modest improvements of approximately 2-4% in accuracy and F1-score over age-agnostic models, which achieved approximately 85% performance. Age-specific modelling demonstrated greater benefits, particularly among older subjects (age≥60), with improvements of approximately 8-12%. Older cohorts generally achieved 12-18% higher performance than younger cohorts, with XGBoost and other ensemble models producing the strongest results. In contrast, younger age-specific models showed lower or more variable performance, suggesting reduced discriminability of two-stage STP features. Statistical analysis identified more pronounced healthy-disordered differences in NREM transitions involving N2 and N3 among older subjects. Age-threshold analysis indicated that discriminability increased from the 50s and was strongest around 55-60 years. These findings suggest that chronological age influences the diagnostic relevance of hypnogram-derived transition features and that age-specific modelling may offer advantages for sleep disorder screening, particularly in older adults. However, independent external and prospective validation remains necessary before clinical implementation.

papers.title: Toward Closed-Loop Cognitive Modulation in Alzheimer's Disease: BCI-Relevant Evidence and a Translational Roadmap.
papers.abstract: Alzheimer's disease (AD) has entered a biomarker-defined era, yet most cognitive and neuromodulatory interventions continue to use fixed targets, timing, and doses. This targeted narrative review maps brain-computer interface (BCI) and closed-loop-relevant evidence in AD and mild cognitive impairment (MCI) by examining how sensing, control, and intervention modules are used prospectively. Read modules include electroencephalography (EEG), functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS), real-time functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI), functional ultrasound (fUS) and transcranial ultrasound localization microscopy (t-ULM), and digital measures. Control functions include feature extraction, within-person state decoding, uncertainty-aware decision rules, target-engagement assessment, and safety oversight. Write modules include neurofeedback, sensory gamma and sleep-phase acoustic stimulation, transcranial alternating-current stimulation (tACS), transcranial direct-current stimulation (tDCS), repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation (rTMS), transcranial pulse stimulation (TPS), transcranial ultrasound stimulation (TUS), transcranial photobiomodulation (tPBM), and focused ultrasound-mediated blood-brain barrier (FUS-BBB) opening. Human studies have separately demonstrated signal-contingent feedback, individualized targeting, physiological target engagement, home delivery, and emerging sensing, while preclinical studies provide mechanistic support for gamma, optical, and ultrasound approaches. Sleep-phase acoustic stimulation additionally demonstrates early automated signal-to-stimulus control. Passive sensing provides observations, personalization sets baseline parameters, state-informed control uses current signals to alter delivery, and target engagement verifies the proximal response without establishing clinical efficacy. Reliable decoding of waking cognitive states, broader controller utility, and durable clinical benefit remain unvalidated. We therefore organize the field around disease context, state sensing, feature extraction, state decoding, bounded decision/intervention, response verification, and safety oversight. The decisive early design compares assignments to an adaptive policy with otherwise matched fixed delivery; a sham arm can additionally test intervention efficacy. Such trials must prespecify decoder calibration, uncertainty, abstention, safety limits, and mechanistic and clinical endpoints. Closed-loop cognitive modulation therefore defines a translational research agenda for AD.

papers.title: Associations of sleep architecture, sleep fragmentation, and hypoxia-related parameters with cognitive frailty in older patients with hypertension and obstructive sleep apnea: a cross-sectional study.
papers.abstract: To investigate the associations of sleep architecture, sleep fragmentation, and nocturnal hypoxia-related parameters with cognitive frailty (CF) in older patients with hypertension and obstructive sleep apnea (OSA). In this single-center cross-sectional study, 240 hospitalized patients aged ≥ 60 years with hypertension and OSA confirmed by polysomnography (PSG) were enrolled between January 2025 and January 2026. Participants were classified into a CF group (n = 83) and a non-CF group (n = 157). Demographic and clinical data were collected. Cognitive frailty was assessed using the Chinese version of the Montreal Cognitive Assessment and the Fried Frailty Phenotype. PSG variables included total sleep time, sleep-stage durations, arousal index, apnea-hypopnea index, oxygen desaturation index, minimum oxygen saturation, and mean oxygen saturation. Multivariable logistic regression was performed to identify factors independently associated with CF. Compared with the non-CF group, the CF group had shorter N3 sleep duration, lower minimum oxygen saturation, and a higher arousal index. After adjustment for sex, age, years of education, and body mass index, N3 sleep duration (OR = 0.988, 95% CI: 0.981-0.996, P = 0.002) and minimum oxygen saturation (OR = 0.945, 95% CI: 0.914-0.977, P < 0.001) were independently negatively associated with CF, whereas arousal index (OR = 1.016, 95% CI: 1.005-1.027, P = 0.005) was independently positively associated with CF. Age was also independently associated with CF. Reduced N3 sleep duration, lower minimum oxygen saturation, and higher arousal index were associated with CF in older patients with hypertension and OSA, supporting the need for prospective studies to clarify temporal relationships.

papers.title: When impulsivity goes wrong: Circadian timing distinguishes which night shift workers succeed and fail.
papers.abstract: Night-shift workers are at increased risk for accidents and injuries, and extant research has focused predominantly on the effect of sleep loss on low-level cognition as a mechanism. Much less is known about the effects of underlying circadian phase on performance, especially as it relates to accident risk. We assessed whether phase angle between circadian timing (dim-light melatonin onset) and task time predicted impulsivity (i.e. action bias, performance, and strategy) in night shift workers. To do this, we used the Stop Light Task, which simulates the complex, and real-world process drivers go through at a stop light (i.e. whether to stop safely or risk going at a yellow light). Thirty night‑shift workers completed the Stop Light Task approximately 13 h after an 8-h in-lab sleep opportunity, and underwent 24 h of hourly saliva collection to assess dim-light melatonin onset (DLMO). Results showed more time between DLMO and task completion (i.e. greater phase angle) was associated with worse performance (i.e. more crashes) and worse overall strategy in the context of risk. Phase angle did not predict action bias (i.e. propensity to run the yellow light), but post-hoc analyses showed greater sleepiness predicted reduced action bias. These results are the first to show circadian processes directly affect impulsivity in night shift workers and determine when someone is likely to be successful or fail in risky situations.

papers.title: Insufficient Sleep, Circadian Targets, Weight Management, and Cardiometabolic Health.
papers.abstract: Insufficient sleep is a potentially modifiable contributor to obesity and cardiometabolic risk, yet sustained sleep extension may be difficult for individuals facing occupational, caregiving, and social constraints. We review emerging literature informing potential timing- and circadian-based strategies that could mitigate obesity risk, even without necessitating an increase in sleep duration. Emerging evidence suggests that the timing of light exposure, food intake, sleep-wake regularity, and physical activity can influence circadian physiology and metabolic health. Insufficient sleep may disrupt these temporal patterns, providing plausible pathways linking insufficient sleep with positive energy balance, weight gain, and metabolic dysfunction. However, few fully powered randomized trials have directly tested the efficacy of interventions targeting these timing-based pathways to mitigate risk of obesity in adults with habitual insufficient sleep. Optimizing the temporal organization of daily behaviors represents a promising complementary approach to obesity prevention and management, especially when increasing sleep duration may not be feasible. However, rigorous trials assessing target engagement, changes in sleep-related outcomes, and clinically meaningful metabolic outcomes are needed.

papers.title: Effects of housing system on locomotor activity and circadian rhythmicity in llamas (Lama glama).
papers.abstract: Precision Livestock Farming technologies provide objective tools to assess animal behavior and welfare under different management conditions, yet their application to South American camelids remains limited. This study evaluated the effects of housing system on locomotor activity and circadian rhythmicity in adult llamas (Lama glama) using accelerometer-derived data. Ten llamas (2 males, 8 females) were monitored during two consecutive phases: a grazing-confinement system, in which animals grazed during the day and were housed at night, and a continuous housing system without access to pasture. Locomotor activity was recorded continuously using neck-mounted triaxial accelerometers, and circadian rhythms were assessed using a 24-h cosinor model. Mean locomotor activity was significantly lower (P < 0.001) during continuous housing compared with the grazing-confinement phase, with reductions of approximately 33% in males and 47% in females. In both sexes and housing systems, locomotor activity exhibited a clear diurnal pattern, with higher activity during the light phase than during the dark phase (P < 0.001). Cosinor analysis revealed significant circadian rhythms with a stable 24-h periodicity and acrophases clustered in the early afternoon. While acrophase timing was not affected by housing system, continuous housing significantly reduced MESOR, amplitude, rhythm robustness, and circadianity indices (P < 0.001). These findings demonstrate that spatial restriction and loss of pasture access constrain locomotor behavior and weaken the temporal organization of activity in llamas, while the persistence of circadian rhythmicity suggests a preserved endogenous timing system. The integration of accelerometry and circadian analysis provides a valuable approach for objective welfare assessment in camelid production systems.

papers.title: Knockdown of KCNQ2 in CA1 reshapes epilepsy-related limbic network rhythms and reduces spontaneous exploratory behavior in mice.
papers.abstract: Circuit-level effects of localized cornu ammonis 1 (CA1) potassium voltage-gated channel subfamily Q member 2 (KCNQ2) loss-of-function on epileptogenesis remain poorly understood, despite the well-established association of KCNQ2 deficiency with epilepsy and neuropsychiatric comorbidities. To examine how CA1-specific KCNQ2 deficiency modulates neural network activity during acquired epileptogenesis, we selectively knocked down KCNQ2 in mouse CA1 via adeno-associated virus (AAV)-short hairpin RNA (shRNA) and explored limbic network alterations. Calcium activity of glutamatergic neurons, gamma-aminobutyric acid (GABA) ergic neurons, somatostatin-positive (SST+) interneurons, and parvalbumin-positive (PV+) interneurons was recorded using cell type-specific GCaMP expression with simultaneous CA1 electroencephalography (EEG). Multi-site EEG recordings from CA1, cornu ammonis 3 (CA3), retrosplenial agranular cortex (RSA), infralimbic cortex (IL), cingulate cortex area 1 (CG1), primary motor cortex (M1), and basolateral amygdala (BLA) were analyzed for spectral power, functional connectivity (FC), and phase-amplitude coupling (PAC). We observed spontaneous activity, novel object recognition, and social behaviors of the model mice. CA1 KCNQ2 knockdown increased calcium activity in all neuronal populations during the latency, with greater activation of SST+ than PV+ interneurons. Excitatory-inhibitory imbalance correlated with seizure severity. EEG analyses revealed a biphasic pattern: reduced low-frequency power, phase synchrony, and FC during the latency, followed by widespread hypersynchronization of power spectral density, mutual information, and phase synchrony during severe seizures. In the non-epileptic state, PAC analysis revealed that knockdown group developed a biased network configuration characterized by enhanced PAC directed toward the BLA and weakened CA3-M1 and M1-related coupling. This pattern was consistent with their behavioral phenotypes, including reduced central exploration, fewer open-arm entries, impaired novel object exploration, and decreased social preference. During generalized seizures, PAC underwent extensive reorganization, with strengthened coupling between the BLA and multiple brain regions and reduced M1-directed coupling. Intraperitoneally administered retigabine (RTG), a pan-KCNQ channel opener, partially alleviated these behavioral deficits and attenuated the abnormally potentiated long-range network activity. CA1 KCNQ2 knockdown not only disrupts the local excitatory/inhibitory balance but also promotes epileptogenesis by reshaping limbic-cortical network coupling patterns.

papers.title: Ideal sleep duration as a potential explanation of the bimodal chronotype: An exploratory study.
papers.abstract: Regarding circadian typology, the existence of a fourth category, the bimodal types, was previously proposed. Bimodal types would be those answering some questions as morning types, while others as evening types, resulting in a different sleep-wake cycle compared to intermediate types. The aim of this study was to further explore the plausibility of this new circadian typology category, attempting to determine whether it qualifies as a genuinely new category of individuals or merely a byproduct of another individual difference, namely ideal sleep duration. To this end, we reanalyzed data previously collected from 1583 children and adolescents (817 females, mean age of 13.13 ± 1.96) and 2115 adults (1144 females, mean age of 44.50 ± 5.64) who completed the Morningness-Eveningness Questionnaire for Children and Adolescents (MEQ-CA) and the MEQ, respectively. The open-ended questions on the ideal bedtime and get-up time were used to compute the ideal total sleep time that was later grouped into three categories: short- (≤6 hours), medium- (6 < x < 12 hours), and long sleepers (≥12 hours). In children and adolescents, bimodal types were overrepresented in both short and long sleepers and underrepresented among medium sleepers; separately considering the gender variable, the same pattern of results was detected in males only. Regarding adults, an overrepresentation of bimodal types was observed among long sleepers and their underrepresentation among medium sleepers; this same distribution was replicated only in males. It seems that the suggested fourth category of circadian typology, that of bimodal types, may be considered as a byproduct of the individual difference in ideal sleep duration.

papers.title: In vivo probabilistic atlas mapping reveals brainstem nuclei volume increases in idiopathic REM sleep behavior disorder.
papers.abstract: Idiopathic rapid eye movement sleep behavior disorder (iRBD) serves as a key prodromal marker of synucleinopathies, and its core symptoms are closely associated with brainstem pathology. Nevertheless, in vivo imaging research on brainstem nuclei in iRBD patients is still limited due to methodological constraints. This study aimed to explore volume changes of brainstem nuclei in iRBD patients via a fine-grained probabilistic atlas, and analyze their clinical correlations and diagnostic value. We enrolled 3D T1-weighted MRI data of 178 iRBD patients and 111 healthy controls from the PPMI database. After preprocessing, 54 brainstem nuclei were segmented using the Brainstem Navigator atlas, and their relative volumes were compared between groups with multiple comparison correction. Correlation analyses with clinical scales and ROC analyses were conducted for nuclei with significant inter-group differences. Compared to HCs, iRBD patients presented significantly enlarged relative volumes in the left cuneiform nucleus, left lateral parabrachial nucleus, and left superior medullary reticular formation. The volumes of the latter two nuclei were positively correlated with RBDSQ scores and related to autonomic, affective and cognitive indicators. The AUC of single nucleus for iRBD diagnosis ranged from 0.607 to 0.637, while the combined model reached 0.674. These findings confirm volumetric enlargement in specific brainstem nuclei of iRBD patients, suggesting early pathological remodeling in these regions. They clarify the brainstem structural basis of iRBD symptoms and suggest that brainstem nuclei volumes, with moderate discriminative performance, may serve as supplementary imaging markers to complement clinical assessments in iRBD.

papers.title: Distinct trajectories of 24-hour sleep duration and subsequent functional limitations in older adults: a national longitudinal cohort study.
papers.abstract: Static sleep duration is a known health determinant, yet the prognostic value of longitudinal 24-hour sleep trajectories for functional deterioration remains understudied. However, whether longitudinal 24-hour sleep trajectories are associated with subsequent overall and severe functional limitations remains unclear. We analysed 4,999 adults aged ≥ 50 years from the China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study (CHARLS), free of baseline functional limitations. Latent class mixed models identified distinct 24-hour sleep duration trajectories over 4 years. We estimated risk ratios (RRs) for ADL and IADL limitations at Wave 5, as well as severe limitations defined as difficulty in two or more tasks. Three trajectories were identified: Stable Moderate (56.5%), Progressively Short (13.5%; ~5.1 h to ~ 3.9 h), and Progressively Long (30.0%; ~8.4 h to ~ 9.2 h). Compared with the Stable Moderate group, the Progressively Short trajectory was associated with higher risks of ADL limitation (RR = 1.34; 95% CI: 1.18-1.52) and IADL limitation (RR = 1.22; 95% CI: 1.08-1.37) at Wave 5, as well as severe ADL limitation. Conversely, the Progressively Long trajectory was not associated with overall ADL or IADL limitations at Wave 5, but was associated with severe ADL and IADL limitations. Longitudinal changes in 24-hour sleep duration were associated with subsequent functional limitations in older adults. Progressively sleep shortening may serve as a marker of functional vulnerability, whereas sleep lengthening may indicate more advanced dependency. These findings support the potential value of sleep trajectories for risk stratification, while causal interpretation requires caution.

papers.title: Exploratory Pilot Randomized Crossover Study of Transcutaneous Vagus Nerve Stimulation on Sleep Quality and Mood in Healthy Adults.
papers.abstract: Transcutaneous vagus nerve stimulation (tcVNS) has been reported to influence autonomic regulation and sleep in various clinical settings. However, evidence in healthy populations is limited. This study investigated the effects of tcVNS on subjective sleep quality, mood, and autonomic function in healthy adults. We conducted a randomized, double-blind, crossover trial in which 29 healthy participants underwent two four-week stimulation phases (Active and Sham). Active stimulation was delivered at subthreshold intensity, whereas Sham stimulation involved identical device use without electrical current. Outcomes included the Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index-Korean version (PSQI-K), Beck Depression Inventory-II (BDI-II), Hamilton Depression Rating Scale (HAM-D), and daily heart rate variability (HRV) indices collected using a validated smartphone-based application. Linear mixed-effects models were used to analyze questionnaire scores. PSQI-K scores showed a statistically significant but modest reduction during Active stimulation compared with Baseline (P = 0.013) and Sham (corrected P < 0.001), although the mean change did not exceed the minimal clinically important difference. No significant changes were observed for BDI-II or HAM-D. HRV responses were heterogeneous across participants, with no significant group-level differences. No serious adverse events occurred, and mild transient ear discomfort or tingling was reported by 3 participants (10.3%) during Active stimulation. This exploratory pilot trial suggests that tcVNS was safe and well tolerated and may produce modest changes in subjective sleep quality in healthy adults. The absence of mood effects likely reflects low baseline symptom burden. These findings provide preliminary, hypothesis-generating evidence that stimulation parameters may warrant further investigation, and confirmation in adequately powered trials and clinical populations is required. papers.title: Diurnal cortisol, perceived sleep quality, actigraphic sleep and depression: an exploratory pilot in patients with head and neck cancer.
papers.abstract: In patients with head and neck cancer (HNC), perceived sleep quality, actigraphy-derived sleep parameters, depressive symptoms, and diurnal cortisol may represent related behavioral and biological processes. This exploratory study tested a priori associations among these constructs. Forty patients with HNC completed the Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (PSQI) and Patient Health Questionnaire-9 (PHQ-9), wore wrist actigraphs, and collected salivary cortisol at waking and bedtime across a 6-day period. Separate linear regressions tested associations of PSQI scores with actigraphic sleep measures with depressive symptoms, and with cortisol slope, waking, evening and mean indices. Post hoc PSQI item analyses used Spearman correlations. Global PSQI scores were not significantly correlated with actigraphic sleep parameters. Poorer perceived sleep quality was associated with higher depression scores (r = 0.64), flatter diurnal cortisol slopes (r = 0.48), and higher evening cortisol (r = 0.40). Actigraphic sleep parameters were not significantly associated with depressive symptoms or cortisol indices, and depressive symptoms were not significantly associated with cortisol indices. Post hoc item-level analyses showed that poorer overall sleep quality and greater difficulty maintaining enthusiasm were associated with greater depressive symptoms, flatter cortisol slopes, and lower waking cortisol. In this exploratory pilot of patients with HNC, poorer sleep quality was associated with greater depressive symptoms, flatter diurnal cortisol slopes, and higher evening cortisol, whereas actigraphic sleep parameters were not. Global PSQI scores may help identify patients warranting further assessment for depression and treatment-related symptoms.

papers.title: Circadian rhythm in the atrioventricular node - in electrophysiology, contractility, metabolism, intracellular signalling and extracellular matrix
papers.abstract: The atrioventricular (AV) node shows a circadian rhythm-during sleep the PR interval is longer (because conduction velocity is decreased) and AV block is more common. We show the rhythm is similar in mouse and human, and using mice we have investigated the cause. There was still a rhythm in Kcnj5 knockout mice ruling out a major role of vagal tone (the vagus regulates the node via Kcnj5). Instead, we show the presence of a functioning circadian clock in the node (e.g. by detection of rhythmic clock transcripts). There was ~43-52% reduction in the rhythm of the PR interval on inhibition of the clock in a Bmal1 knockout mouse. There was a significant rhythm in >300 intracellular signalling molecules presumably driven by the clock and perhaps extrinsic signals. Downstream of the clock and signalling molecules, there was a rhythm in many transcripts and proteins (of 4,186 proteins, ~15% had a rhythm), responsible for example for contractile machinery, metabolism, extracellular matrix, and importantly ion channels. Ultimately, the PR interval is determined by ion channels, and there were rhythms in ion channels and ionic currents. A key determinant of conduction velocity is the upstroke velocity of the Ca2+-dependent nodal action potential and this was significantly reduced during sleep, this can be explained by reduced expression of Ca2+ channel subunits and a smaller L-type Ca2+ current at this time and this was confirmed by biophysically-detailed computer modelling. In conclusion, there is day-night molecular remodelling of the AV node and this is largely responsible for the circadian rhythm in the PR interval.

Rhythmic transcripts, proteins (~15% of 4,186), ion channels, and reduced L-type Ca2+ current during sleep, supported by computer modeling, were found to underlie slowed nodal conduction at night.

papers.title: Immediate Return or Overnight Stay? Sleep Responses by Postmatch Travel Strategy and Match Participation in Professional Football.
papers.abstract: Late European away fixtures can disrupt sleep, but the influence of immediate return versus overnight stay, and whether responses differ by match participation, remains unclear. Postmatch travel strategy would influence sleep quality and duration across the prematch, match, and subsequent nights, with responses moderated by match participation. Observational repeated-measures field study. Level 3. A total of 19 outfield English Premier League players were monitored across 10 European away fixtures (5 immediate return and 5 overnight stay). Self-reported sleep quality (1 to 7) and sleep duration were recorded on the prematch, match, and subsequent nights. Fixed-effects models examined condition, time, and match participation, with standard errors clustered by player. Sleep quality was lower than prematch baseline on the match and subsequent nights (both β = -0.62 arbitrary units [AU]; P < 0.01; g = -0.63). After overnight stay, sleep quality improved from the match to the subsequent night in players who participated and those who did not (β = 0.69 and 0.63 AU; 95% CIs, 0.37-0.90 and 0.47-0.91; P < 0.01), whereas no change occurred after immediate return. Across participation groups, sleep duration was lower after overnight stay than immediate return on the match night (β = -1.94 hours; P < 0.01; g = -1.26) and subsequent night (β = -1.02 hours; P = 0.02; g = -0.67). However, after overnight stay, sleep duration increased between these nights by 1.45 hours in participants and 1.43 hours in nonparticipants (P < 0.01), with no significant change after immediate return. Participation moderated sleep duration on both postfixture nights (β = 1.27 and 1.64 hours; P ≤ 0.04; g = 0.82 and 1.07). Neither travel strategy was uniformly superior. Overnight stay was associated with poorer absolute sleep duration but a clearer next-night rebound in sleep quality and duration. Postmatch travel should be planned case by case, considering itinerary, next-day demands, and individual match exposure rather than applying a single team-wide policy.

papers.title: Flavonoids quercetin and fisetin activate circadian clock and inhibit adipocyte development and hypertrophy.
papers.abstract: The circadian clock maintains temporal control of metabolic processes and plays a key role in adipocyte development. RORα is a circadian clock-regulatory nuclear receptor with diverse metabolic functions. However, the role of the RORα-clock axis in adipocyte biology and its potential as a therapeutic target for obesity remains to be explored. Here, we report how RORα modulation impacts adipocyte development, and identify flavonoid compounds, quercetin and fisetin, as RORα-activating molecules that inhibits adipocyte maturation. Activation of RORα by a synthetic agonist or ectopic expression was sufficient to inhibit adipogenesis. Interestingly, quercetin and fisetin robustly stimulated RORα transcriptional activity and enhanced clock oscillation. Both compounds suppressed preadipocyte differentiation and lipid storage in mature adipocytes that are partially dependent on clock regulation. In vivo administration of quercetin or fisetin resulted in marked RORα induction in adipose depots, accompanied by strong suppression of adipogenic and lipogenic programs. While quercetin attenuated adipocyte hypertrophy with lowering of free fatty acids and improved insulin sensitivity, fisetin displayed a less pronounced effect with differential regulation of lipolytic pathways. Collectively, our findings demonstrate that quercetin and fisetin activate the RORα-clock regulatory axis to suppress adipocyte development, suggesting their potential for clock-targeted interventions in metabolic diseases.

papers.title: Adoption of Routine Intraoperative Raw EEG at a Quaternary Pediatric Centre.
papers.abstract: Intraoperative electroencephalography (EEG) allows real-time assessment of the anesthetic state of the brain and offers a means of titrating anesthetic delivery in children. Randomized trials have shown that EEG-guided titration reduces anesthetic exposure, shortens emergence and recovery, and lowers the incidence of emergence delirium, yet routine use outside research settings has remained largely confined to enthusiastic clinicians and clinical trials. To describe the adoption of routine intraoperative raw EEG monitoring over time at a quaternary pediatric hospital, to characterize practice variation among anesthesia providers, and to identify patient and procedural factors associated with EEG use. We conducted a retrospective single-center study of anesthetic records in the electronic health record from 17 October 2024, when automated EEG capture began, to 30 June 2026, following departmental implementation of routine raw EEG monitoring. Providers were categorized by EEG use as high (> 40% of cases), moderate (20%-40%) or low (< 20%). Trend, provider-level, and procedural associations with EEG use were examined using segmented regression, mixed-effects logistic regression, and clustered logistic regression. Of 26 168 analyzed cases, 21.7% (5674) involved intraoperative EEG monitoring, provided by 59 staff anesthesiologists, 9 senior fellows, 24 fellows, and 102 residents. EEG use rose from 17.8% of cases in October 2024 to 28.4% in June 2026. Use varied widely among staff anesthesiologists (median 18.1%, IQR 12.3%-31.3%; range 0.9%-79.5%); 59.3% (35/59) were low users, and 18.6% (11/59) were high users, with the five highest users accounting for 27.0% of all EEG-monitored cases managed by staff. Case mix explained only a small proportion of this variation (pseudo R2 = 0.064). EEG-monitored cases were more often longer, involved neuromuscular blockade, TIVA maintenance, cardiac surgery, and trainee presence. Adoption of routine raw EEG monitoring increased steadily but nonlinearly following implementation. Variation in use among providers was only weakly explained by case mix, indicating that individual practice patterns, more than patient or procedural characteristics, drove uptake. Efforts to broaden EEG monitoring may benefit from targeting low-use providers and during fellowship training.

papers.title: Development and EEG Assessment of a Virtual Reality Replica of a Prior Real Multisensory Environment Intervention.
papers.abstract: Multisensory environments (MSEs) are valuable therapeutic spaces for relaxation and stress relief, yet high costs and physical infrastructure limit accessibility. Immersive virtual reality MSEs (V-MSEs) offer a low-cost and scalable alternative to real MSEs (R-MSEs), but evidence is scarce. The aim of this study is an exploratory characterization of the electroencephalography (EEG) response to a V-MSE replica of a previous R-MSE intervention, using the original R-MSE data as a qualitative reference. After developing a V-MSE mirroring the original environment, 31 healthy participants underwent an adapted version of the protocol, and spectral and nonlinear features were computed from EEG recordings pre- and post-intervention. Analyses were performed within each environment, and comparisons between them remained qualitative. The alpha/beta ratio, negatively correlated with stress, was the only feature significantly increased in both conditions. In the V-MSE, frontal theta and the theta/beta ratio also increased significantly, whereas relative gamma power and Lempel-Ziv complexity decreased. Only in R-MSE, parieto-occipital alpha power rose significantly, whereas frontal delta power decreased. No feature changed significantly in opposite directions between settings. Evidence remains insufficient to establish V-MSEs as an alternative to R-MSEs, but this first EEG characterization of a V-MSE is encouraging enough to justify broader studies.

papers.title: Component specific sleep-cognition associations in ICU professionals in India.
papers.abstract: Rotating shift work in intensive care units (ICUs) disrupts circadian alignment and sleep homeostasis, impairing cognition. Global sleep and cognitive scores may obscure component- and domain-specific effects, and testing multiple sleep components against multiple cognitive domains risks false-positive findings unless corrected. To examine associations between individual Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (PSQI) components and item-level Montreal Cognitive Assessment (MoCA) performance in ICU healthcare workers, with multiple-comparison correction and adjustment for confounders. Cross-sectional study in a tertiary hospital in eastern India. Forty-five ICU professionals working rotating shifts completed the PSQI (seven components, scored continuously) and MoCA (eight item scores plus one derived composite). Spearman correlations were computed for all 63 pairs, with Benjamini-Hochberg false discovery rate correction within each PSQI-component family. Associations reaching nominal significance were tested in multivariable linear regression adjusted for age, sex, occupation and ICU experience, with robust standard errors and bootstrap confidence intervals. Five of 63 correlations reached nominal significance (P < 0.05). Only daytime dysfunction with the attention-executive composite survived both correction and adjustment (rho = -0.43, corrected P = 0.026; adjusted beta = -0.94, 95% CI -1.50 to -0.38, P < 0.001; adjusted R-squared = 0.31). Sleep latency with digit span and sleep medication use with trail making persisted after adjustment but not after correction. Only daytime dysfunction was associated with cognitive performance, specifically attention-executive performance, after both correction for multiple testing and adjustment for confounders, supporting a targeted rather than global approach to sleep-related cognitive risk in critical care.

The authors argue for a component-specific rather than global approach to sleep-related cognitive risk in critical care staff.

papers.title: SIRT7 Aggravates Chronic Sleep Deprivation-Induced Cognitive Impairment and Neuronal Apoptosis via Decreasing Succinylation and Cascaded Ubiquitylation of NFL.
papers.abstract: Insomnia affected one-third of the global population, but its molecular mechanism was not clarified. A chronic sleep deprivation (CSD) model was constructed in SD rats using multiple platforms over water. Hippocampal tissues were collected for ubiquitinomics and succinylomics. Sirtuin 7 (SIRT7) inhibitor was administered to elevate succinylation levels. Molecular experiments demonstrated the cascade reaction of succinylation and ubiquitylation, and Neurofilament Light (NFL)-binding ubiquitinating enzyme. Chronic sleep deprivation caused cognitive disorder of rats. Mostly, succinylation and ubiquitylation displayed a downregulated trend in the CSD group, especially double modification of NFL at K370 (succinylation site) and K267/281 (ubiquitylation site), whose protein level was upregulated in CSD rats. NFL was proved to be a target of SIRT7, a well-known desuccinylase. SIRT7 inhibitor weakened cognitive deficit, blocked neuronal apoptosis, decreased NFL expression, and increased succinylation and ubiquitylation levels, which were inverse in the CSD model and cells infected with SIRT7 overexpression adenovirus. SIRT7 suppressed not only succinylation but also ubiquitylation through K370 of NFL. Knockdown of NFL receded cognitive disorder and neuronal apoptosis. BRCA1 Associated Deubiquitinase 1 (BAP1) inhibited NFL ubiquitylation and subsequently degradation. SIRT7 inhibitor promoted succinylation and cascaded ubiquitylation, as well as disrupting the interaction between BAP1 and NFL, finally suppressing CSD.

SIRT7 inhibition or NFL knockdown attenuated these deficits, implicating SIRT7-NFL succinylation/ubiquitylation in insomnia-related cognitive decline.

papers.title: Bridging the Gender Gap in Obstructive Sleep Apnea: A Machine Learning Approach to Screening Women for Moderate-to-Severe Disease.
papers.abstract: Obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) can lead to severe complications if left untreated. Several challenges hinder OSA identification in females, resulting in underdiagnosis and undertreatment in this population. This study aimed to develop a machine learning (ML) approach specifically tailored to screen women for moderate-to-severe OSA. A retrospective study was conducted using clinical records of 1,210 women who underwent polysomnography at our institution. Collected data included demographics, body metrics, nocturnal oxygen saturation levels, medical conditions, medications, laboratory measurements, and polysomnography results. Four ML algorithms were employed to classify participants into moderate-to-severe and none-to-mild OSA groups. Due to the high missingness of laboratory values in the whole cohort, two sets of models were developed: one utilizing all subjects but excluding lab tests, and another restricted to a subgroup of 383 participants that additionally incorporated hemoglobin and lipid profile alongside the other features. Without laboratory measurements, the best-performing model was adaptive boosting, which achieved an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve and accuracy of 0.811 and 76.03%, respectively. When lab tests were included, gradient boosting machine outperformed its competitors, with the above metrics reaching 0.872 and 84.42%, respectively. The promising performance of our approach underlines the potential of artificial intelligence in refining screening strategies for OSA in women. Nadir oxygen saturation during sleep emerged as a particularly strong predictor, reinforcing the central role of nocturnal hypoxemia in OSA risk stratification. Future research should focus on incorporating broader clinical inputs and using larger, diverse datasets to develop a highly accurate, robust model that meets clinical standards and is suitable for real-world implementation.

papers.title: Sleep Deprivation Exacerbates Pulpal Inflammation and Impairs Repair Through Dysregulated Neutrophil Activity in Rats.
papers.abstract: To investigate the effects of sleep deprivation on pulpal inflammation and repair and determine the contribution of neutrophil activity to these changes in rat models. Sleep deprivation was induced in rats using a modified multiple platform method. Pulp responses were evaluated using three experimental settings. Under baseline conditions, rats underwent acute sleep deprivation for four consecutive days. In the inflammatory model, pulpitis was induced by lipopolysaccharide (LPS) and assessed 1-4 days after induction. In the reparative model, direct pulp capping (DPC) was performed and pulpal healing was assessed at 14 and 28 days during sleep deprivation. Histological, vascular and inflammatory changes were evaluated by haematoxylin and eosin staining, Masson's trichrome staining, immunohistochemistry and immunofluorescence. Transcriptomic alterations in pulp tissue were analysed by mRNA sequencing. Neutrophil abundance and activation were assessed in peripheral blood and dental pulp by complete blood counts, flow cytometry and myeloperoxidase staining. To investigate the functional contribution of neutrophils and neutrophil elastase (NE), sleep-deprived rats were treated with the neutrophil-depleting antibody or the NE inhibitor Sivelestat. Sleep deprivation disrupted pulpal homeostasis, inducing vascular alterations and inflammatory cell infiltration. Following DPC, sleep-deprived rats exhibited impaired repair, including incomplete hard tissue bridge formation and reduced osteopontin expression at Day 14, followed by pulpal necrosis and apical periodontitis at Day 28. In the LPS-induced pulpitis model, sleep deprivation accelerated inflammatory progression and increased pulpal necrosis and leukocyte accumulation. Transcriptomic analysis revealed enrichment of immune- and neutrophil-associated pathways. Sleep deprivation increased neutrophil abundance, accumulation and activation in dental pulp, accompanied by elevated NE expression and enhanced neutrophil extracellular trap-like signals. Neutrophil depletion attenuated pulpal inflammation and tissue injury, while pharmacological inhibition of NE reduced inflammatory responses and pulpal tissue damage. Sleep deprivation exacerbates pulpal inflammation and impairs repair, at least in part through enhanced neutrophil activity and NE-mediated tissue injury. These findings reveal a mechanistic link between sleep disturbance and dysregulated pulpal inflammation and suggest neutrophil/NE-associated pathways as potential targets for further investigation.

papers.title: A novel theta-frequency tACS approach for major depressive disorder: Initial findings from an open-label pilot study.
papers.abstract: Theta oscillations are implicated in the pathophysiology of major depressive disorder (MDD) and represent a promising neuromodulation target. This study investigates individualized theta-frequency (ITF) transcranial alternating current stimulation (tACS) in adults with moderate-to-severe MDD, and reports on the initial evaluation of feasibility, tolerability, and clinical and neurophysiological outcomes. In this open-label pilot study, adults with MDD underwent a 20-session course of theta-frequency tACS (1.5 mA peak-to-peak; 20 min/session) applied bilaterally over the prefrontal cortex while performing working memory tasks. Theta stimulation frequency was individualized from pretreatment task-based electroencephalography (EEG) and recalibrated after 10 sessions. Montgomery-Asberg Depression Rating Scale (MADRS) and EEG were assessed at baseline, midpoint (2weeks), and endpoint (4weeks), with MADRS repeated at 4-week follow-up. Ten of 11 enrolled participants completed all 20 treatment sessions and were included in analyses. Reported side effects were mild and transient. MADRS scores decreased significantly from baseline to midpoint, endpoint, and follow-up. At endpoint, response and remission rates were 80% and 60%, respectively; at follow-up, rates were 80% and 70% respectively. Greater increases in individualized theta frequency (ITF) power were associated with greater reductions in MADRS scores, although no significant group-level changes in ITF power were observed. The open-label design, absence of a sham comparator, and small sample size warrant cautious interpretation of these initial observations, particularly given the potential influence of placebo and expectancy effects. This pilot evaluation of individualized theta-frequency tACS in MDD demonstrates the feasibility of this novel approach and provides preliminary clinical and neurophysiological observations to inform future sham-controlled trials.

papers.title: Report-derived interictal epileptiform discharge burden is associated with 7-day antiseizure medication decisions after pediatric video electroencephalography.
papers.abstract: To determine whether a three-level interictal epileptiform discharge (IED) burden abstracted from qualitative wording in issued pediatric video electroencephalography (VEEG) reports, rather than directly measured spike frequency, was associated with antiseizure medication (ASM) decisions within 7 days. This single-center retrospective cohort included 216 VEEG report episodes from 181 children. Two reviewers independently classified each report as showing no, low, or moderate-to-high IED burden while unaware of the standardized 7-day outcome; disagreements were adjudicated. We separately analyzed a diagnostic/initiation cohort for new ASM initiation and an established-epilepsy cohort for exploratory treatment intensification. Associations were assessed using exact and trend tests and logistic regression with patient-clustered robust standard errors. Agreement was 211/216 (97.7%); linear-weighted Cohen κ was 0.975 (patient-clustered bootstrap 95% CI 0.947-0.995). The diagnostic/initiation cohort comprised 113 reports from 112 children, with 36 new ASM initiations. Initiation rates were 13.0%, 42.9%, and 70.0% for no, low, and moderate-to-high burden, respectively (trend p < 0.001). The adjusted odds ratio per higher burden grade was 2.89 (95% CI 1.58-5.30; p < 0.001). The established-epilepsy cohort comprised 103 reports from 76 children, with 13 intensification events. Moderate-to-high burden versus none/low yielded an odds ratio of 4.73 (95% CI 1.31-17.08; p = 0.018), but complementary analyses were not statistically significant. Report-derived IED burden showed a strong graded association with new ASM initiation within 7 days. The treatment-intensification finding was exploratory. These data describe prescribing context and do not establish causality, treatment benefit, or an IED-based treatment threshold.

papers.title: Evidence for decoder-label-regime-dependent effects of complementary leaky integrate-and-fire temporal-state decoding in motor-imagery EEG.
papers.abstract: Motor-imagery electroencephalography often provides limited subject-specific supervision. This study tested whether complementary leaky integrate-and-fire (CLIF)-family temporal-state decoding shows a decoder-level advantage after the EEG representation is fixed, how that advantage changes with decoder-label availability, and whether hard binary spikes are required. ANN-SEW, the artificial neural network comparator with spike-element-wise (SEW) residual topology, and SEW-CLIF received identical frozen attention-based temporal convolutional network (ATCNet) and filter-bank convolutional network (FBCNet) representations. The evidence chain combined BCI Competition IV Dataset 2a (BCI2a) development, retrospective OpenBMI replication, an internally pre-access-held-out BCI Competition IV Dataset 2b (BCI2b) evaluation, cross-entropy-only label-budget analyses, and a separate internally pre-access-locked BNCI2015-001 Session-A-to-Session-B evaluation. Additional robustness analyses included shared whole-sequence readout for parameter-matched gated recurrent unit (GRU) and temporal convolutional network (TCN) decoders, exact-gradient sigmoid-gated Soft-CLIF, equal optimizer-update budgets, a within-BCI2a binary sensitivity analysis, and computational profiling. Under cross-entropy-only training, SEW-CLIF exceeded ANN-SEW by 10.082 percentage points (pp) on BCI2a and 5.470 pp. on OpenBMI, while full-budget BCI2b remained near parity (+0.181 pp). The ANN-relative gap decreased as decoder labels increased and persisted under equal-update training. At 25 labels/class, exact-gradient Soft-CLIF exceeded ANN-SEW by 11.085, 8.479, and 5.809 pp. on BCI2a, BCI2b, and OpenBMI, respectively. With matched whole-sequence readout, hard SEW-CLIF was broadly comparable to GRU-Stat and TCN-Stat on BCI2a and BCI2b and modestly higher on OpenBMI. The internally pre-access-locked BNCI2015-001 evaluation showed the same attenuation, with a slope of -2.319 pp. per label doubling (95% CI, -4.118 to -0.604). CLIF-family temporal-state dynamics show a reproducible decoder-label-regime effect under frozen supervised representations. Hard forward discretization is not required for the ANN-relative effect, and matched temporal readout substantially reduces differences between CLIF and other continuous temporal decoders.

papers.title: Neurophysiological and Sleep-Related Effects of a Cosmetic Shampoo and Conditioner Regimen in Adults with Scalp Discomfort: A Pilot Study.
papers.abstract: Scalp discomfort is prevalent and associated with impaired quality of life and sleep disturbance. Although pruritus is linked to neurophysiological alterations and sleep disruption, these effects of cosmetic scalp care remain unexplored. This pilot study evaluated the neurophysiological and sleep-related effects of a cosmetic shampoo and conditioner regimen in adults with scalp discomfort and mild sleep disturbances. This observational pilot study enrolled 21 adults with scalp discomfort and sleep difficulties, of whom 20 were analyzed. After 1 baseline week and 1 washout week, participants used the cosmetic shampoo and conditioner at least three times weekly for 2 weeks. Neurophysiological outcomes were assessed with electroencephalography (EEG; arousal, valence, sleepiness, and anger levels) at baseline, post-washout, week 3, and week 4. Sleep was evaluated with the Stanford Sleepiness Scale, Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index, Epworth Sleepiness Scale, Insomnia Severity Index, and Fitbit Inspire 2 tracking. Scalp discomfort was assessed with a clinical report form. Data were analyzed using linear mixed-effects models. During the second reflective question set (Q2), EEG analysis showed significant improvements in mood valence (p < 0.001) and sleepiness (p = 0.021); arousal and anger levels did not change significantly. All four validated sleep questionnaires improved significantly: morning sleepiness decreased by 11.9% (p = 0.011) and overall sleep difficulty by 23.5% (p < 0.001) at week 3 and daytime sleepiness by 30.7% (p < 0.001) and insomnia severity by 35.9% (p < 0.001) at week 4. In an exploratory post hoc subgroup with below-average baseline deep sleep (n = 9), wearable tracking showed a 20.6% increase in deep sleep duration (p = 0.016); no significant change was observed in the full sample. Scalp itch intensity decreased by 49.1% (p < 0.001) and weekly discomfort days by 40.6% (p < 0.001). In this single-arm pilot study, use of the regimen was associated with improved scalp discomfort and with neurophysiological and sleep-related changes. Combining EEG, wearable tracking, and validated sleep instruments may offer a more objective framework for evaluating cosmetic scalp care. The deep sleep finding is hypothesis generating only. This study was retrospectively registered on 25 June 2026 on ClinicalTrials.gov identifier NCT07680608.

papers.title: Joint associations of sleep duration and screen time with mental health symptoms among 10,620 Chinese university students: An exploratory cross-sectional dose-response analysis.
papers.abstract: Psychological distress is common among university students and is associated with modifiable lifestyle factors. This study examined the joint associations of sleep duration and screen time with mental health symptoms and explored whether physical activity (PA) dose-response patterns varied across sleep-screen profiles. A cross-sectional study was conducted among 10,620 Chinese university students (mean age 19.8 ± 1.3 years). Sleep timing, screen time, and PA were assessed using self-report questionnaires, and depression, anxiety, and stress symptoms were assessed using the DASS-21. Multivariable logistic regression and restricted cubic spline models were used to estimate associations and explore dose-response patterns. Prevalence rates were 43.7% for depression, 40.7% for anxiety, and 17.6% for stress symptoms. Combined short sleep (<7.0 h/day) and high screen time (>8.0 h/day) was associated with higher odds of depression (OR = 1.68), anxiety (OR = 1.86), and stress symptoms (OR = 2.31) than the reference profile (7.0-9.0 h sleep and < 4.0 h screen time). Exploratory PA dose-response patterns varied across sleep-screen profiles, with substantial uncertainty in several subgroups. Short sleep and high screen time were jointly associated with higher odds of psychological symptoms. Context-specific PA curve features were exploratory and require confirmation in longitudinal and intervention studies before they can inform behavioral recommendations.

papers.title: Distinct cortical functional network alterations in internet gaming disorder and alcohol use disorder: A resting-state EEG graph theory analysis.
papers.abstract: Internet gaming disorder (IGD) and alcohol use disorder (AUD) are characterized by compulsive behaviors and impaired impulse control. Although IGD is classified as a behavioral addiction and AUD as a substance use disorder, previous studies have suggested potential neurophysiological similarities between the two conditions. However, the frequency-specific topological organization of cortical networks in IGD and AUD remains poorly understood. This study compared the cortical functional networks in IGD and AUD using resting-state electroencephalography (EEG) and graph theory-based network analysis. A total of 151 subjects (49 patients with IGD, 48 with AUD, and 54 healthy controls (HCs)) participated in this study. Resting-state EEG data were preprocessed, followed by source reconstruction and network analysis. We examined global and nodal network characteristics across different frequency bands. At the global network level, IGD exhibited a significantly higher clustering coefficient (CC) and strength (weighted degree) in the beta frequency band compared to AUD and HCs. At the nodal level, the IGD group displayed significantly increased beta-band CCs and strengths in multiple brain regions, particularly the parietal and limbic areas. Notably, beta-band nodal CC and strength in the bilateral superior frontal gyri were significantly lower in AUD than in IGD. Beta-band nodal CC and strength measures showed nominal associations with AUDIT or IAT scores. Our findings suggest that IGD and AUD exhibit distinct cortical network patterns. The results provide further neurophysiological evidence distinguishing IGD, as an example of behavioral addiction, from alcohol-related substance addiction.

papers.title: The endothelial PECAM1-CXCR4 axis amplifies neutrophil degranulation to exacerbate sleep-deprived periodontitis: a systems-level framework for comorbidity therapy.
papers.abstract: Sleep deprivation (SD), a global public health issue, induces systemic low-grade inflammation and vascular endothelial dysfunction, and is a confirmed risk factor for periodontitis (PD). PD is driven by vascular-immune imbalance and excessive neutrophil activation/degranulation, yet the molecular mechanism linking SD-induced systemic changes to local periodontal inflammation remains unclear, leaving a lack of precise therapeutic targets for SD-PD comorbidity. Here, we conducted a systems-level study integrating population epidemiology (NHANES/KNHANES), clinical sample validation, multi-omics bioinformatics analysis, and in vitro/in vivo models. We screened SD-PD core hub genes via WGCNA, DEG and disease target mining, elucidated their regulatory role in neutrophil degranulation with cellular models, and identified candidate dual-target agents by molecular docking/MDS, then validated the candidate drug's efficacy in SD-PD comorbidity mice with multiple detection techniques. We first confirmed in human cohorts and mouse models that SD exacerbates neutrophil-mediated periodontal bone loss. Integrative bioinformatic analysis pinpointed endothelial PECAM1 and neutrophil CXCR4 as key molecules. Mechanistically, we reveal that under inflammatory conditions, endothelial PECAM1 can physically interact with CXCL12, potentially acting as a molecular sink that influences its local availability. This ligand scarcity triggers a compensatory upregulation of its receptor, CXCR4, on neutrophils. Consequently, these primed neutrophils become hyper-reactive, leading to excessive degranulation and tissue destruction upon stimulation. Leveraging this mechanism, we computationally identified and experimentally validated curcumin as a dual-functional modulator of PECAM1 and CXCR4. In our comorbidity mouse model, curcumin not only blocked this pathological axis to mitigate periodontal destruction but also associated with partial recovery of NREM sleep architecture, possibly through mitigation of systemic inflammation. Our findings establish the PECAM1-CXCR4 axis as a critical, druggable pathway in sleep-inflammation comorbidity and provide a conceptual framework for treating complex systemic-local disorders.

papers.title: [Weight Management Strategies for Children and Adolescents: From Behavioral Correction to Systematic Prevention and Control].
papers.abstract: Overweight and obesity among children and adolescents have become a major public health problem, and the prevention and control strategies are shifting from traditional individual-based behavioral interventions toward systematic, multisectoral collaborative paradigms. Using a three-level nested model of individuals, the environment, and policies as the analytical framework, we systematically summarized in this review the connotation and evidence of Intensive Health Behavior and Lifestyle Treatment (IHBLT). We also analyzed the core challenges, including balancing weight reduction with growth and development, identifying sarcopenic obesity, conducting multi-component assessment of appropriate weight, and understanding the modulatory role of sleep health. The pathways for establishing a multisectoral collaborative system of prevention and control were discussed. On this basis, it was proposed that 3 major scientific questions should be prioritized in future efforts to prevent and control obesity among children and adolescents in China: (1) establishing a localized IHBLT dose-response model to address the challenges of adapting, to local cultural, resource, and technological contexts, the Western standard of 26 or more hours of face-to-face, family-based, multicomponent treatment over a 3- to 12-month period; (2) introducing metabolically healthy obesity (MHO) and metabolically unhealthy obesity (MUO) phenotyping for stratified assessment to avoid overtreatment of children with simple obesity; and (3) using longitudinal data from routine school physical examinations to develop dynamic growth trajectory early-warning algorithms, thereby shifting from single cross-sectional screening to individualized trajectory monitoring. This review aims to provide a reference for building an integrated, full-course management continuum encompassing prevention, screening, diagnosis, treatment, and rehabilitation and for advancing the focus from treating existing disease toward preventing disease before its onset.

papers.title: Mediators of the association between physical activity and depressive symptoms in youth: a systematic review and meta-analytic structural equation modelling.
papers.abstract: Physical activity is consistently associated with fewer depressive symptoms in young people, yet the mechanisms underlying this association remain unclear. This systematic review and meta-analytic structural equation modelling (MASEM) study aimed to identify potential mediators linking physical activity with depressive symptoms in youth and quantitatively synthesise repeatedly examined mediation pathways. Six electronic databases were searched for observational quantitative studies examining physical activity, potential mediators, and depressive symptoms in children, adolescents, and young adults within a prespecified eligibility range of 6-27 years. Potential mediators were synthesised narratively and categorised into conceptually related domains. A random-effects meta-analysis was conducted within the mediation-focused quantitative subset, followed by two-stage random-effects MASEM for mediator constructs with sufficient independent studies and complete correlation data. Eighty-seven studies were included in the broader systematic review, of which 80 formally examined at least one mediator and 39 contributed to the quantitative evidence base. Within this mediation-focused quantitative subset, physical activity was, on average, inversely associated with depressive symptoms (r = -0.234, 95% CI -0.281 to -0.187), although heterogeneity was substantial (I2 = 98.29%) and the 95% prediction interval included zero (-0.499 to 0.070). Narrative synthesis identified potential pathways involving psychological resources and self-related perceptions, social factors, behavioural and lifestyle factors, cognitive-emotional processes, maladaptive behavioural factors, and physical or neurobiological factors. Construct-specific MASEM supported statistical indirect associations through psychological resilience (ab = -0.108, 95% CI -0.172 to -0.061), self-esteem (ab = -0.134, 95% CI -0.239 to -0.062), and social support (ab = -0.127, 95% CI -0.220 to -0.059). Sleep quality showed a significant indirect association in an exploratory model based on three studies. Psychological resilience, self-esteem, and social support emerged as repeatedly examined candidate pathways linking physical activity with depressive symptoms. However, the predominantly cross-sectional and just-identified MASEM models cannot establish temporal ordering, and alternative-direction analyses indicated that at least the resilience correlation structure was also compatible with a reverse indirect pathway. The findings should therefore be interpreted as statistical indirect associations rather than established causal mechanisms. https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/recorddashboard, identifier (CRD420261355504).

papers.title: Harnessing Circadian Resilience for Demand-Flexible Controlled Environment Agriculture
papers.abstract: The increasing penetration of renewable electricity generation creates opportunities for flexible demand-side energy management in Total Controlled Environment Agriculture (TCEA), where artificial lighting represents a major operational cost. However, the biological consequences of demand-responsive lighting strategies remain poorly understood. Here, we investigated whether photoperiods can be dynamically adjusted to minimise economic costs or maximise renewable energy utilisation while maintaining crop productivity. Using historical electricity market and wind-generation data, we evaluated three demand-flexing strategies: short-term demand-side response (DSR) events, cost-optimised photoperiods aligned with low electricity prices, and wind-optimised photoperiods aligned with periods of high renewable generation. Despite substantial variation in photoperiod length, plants maintained robust circadian rhythms under both cost- and wind-optimised regimes, demonstrating considerable resilience of the circadian system to irregular environmental timing. Commercial-scale trials involving basil, lettuce, mustard greens and rocket revealed that demand-flexed lighting regimes had minimal effects on harvested fresh or dry weight. Our findings demonstrate that TCEA can provide meaningful demand-side flexibility and support renewable energy integration without substantial reductions in crop productivity. Circadian resilience appears to buffer plants against fluctuating photoperiods, providing a biological foundation for the deployment of demand-flexible lighting strategies in future low-carbon agricultural systems.

papers.title: Comparing Fatigue Assessment Tools in Hemodialysis: Implications for Nephrology Practice From the Technology Assisted Stepped-Collaborative-Care Trial.
papers.abstract: Fatigue is a debilitating symptom experienced by patients treated with hemodialysis (HD). The standardized outcomes in nephrology-hemodialysis fatigue (SONG-HD-fatigue) and patient-reported outcome measurement information system (PROMIS-fatigue) instruments have not been used extensively among patients treated with HD. Our study evaluated the psychometric properties and treatment response of these measures compared to the commonly used functional assessment of chronic illness therapy-fatigue (FACIT-F) in HD. Technology assisted stepped-collaborative-care was a randomized controlled trial to evaluate the effectiveness of a stepped-collaborative-care intervention for symptom management in HD. Participants were adult patients receiving in-center 3-times-weekly maintenance HD at 14 dialysis units. We compared the performance of the SONG-HD-fatigue (3 items) and PROMIS-fatigue (7 items) against the FACIT-F (13 items) by evaluating their comparative psychometric performance (known-groups validity, convergent and divergent validity, screening utility, within-patient reliability, and responsiveness to treatment). Among participants (N =160; age 57.8 years, 35% female, 27% Black, and 15 % Hispanic), the median baseline FACIT-F score was 44. Patients experiencing higher baseline fatigue levels demonstrated significantly lower social support, physical function, physical activity, and sleep quality, and increased pain intensity, pain interference, depression, and anxiety. SONG-HD-fatigue and PROMIS-fatigue had similar direction and strength of correlations as FACIT-F with these outcomes. A SONG-HD-fatigue score of 4.5 and a PROMIS-fatigue score of 56.8 corresponded to a FACIT-F score of 30 for screening for clinically significant fatigue. The mean difference between the technology assisted stepped-collaborative-care intervention and control group at the 3-month primary outcome timepoint was significant for the PROMIS-fatigue and FACIT-F measures but not for the SONG-HD fatigue. Small sample size. SONG-HD-fatigue and PROMIS-fatigue had strong correlations with the validated FACIT-F questionnaire, suggesting that they can be helpful screening measures to identify patients treated with HD with significant fatigue. However, they were not as sensitive in capturing response to treatment.
